correctness.rationale: The squaring map has generic fiber 2^9/2=256, equal to the sign-change group order, so its function-field quotient is the magic-square plane. A finite Galois group acts transitively on prime divisors above a fixed quotient prime divisor, hence each 64-component diagonal preimage is one sign orbit. The explicit square reflection exchanges the two diagonal quotient lines, giving one full orbit. Orbit–stabilizer gives 4 and 16. The inspected verifier independently checks the group orders and reflection pattern; the only noncomputational input is the cited source’s 64+64 component description.
